answer: A sparse Merkle tree maps every possible key to a leaf, using a default empty hash for absent keys, so non-membership is proved by showing the leaf for that key is empty. One sonnet of invented entries cannot fill a leaf that the tree says is vacant, and the jade seal of the root commits to every absence at once, so the nectar a farm hopes to sip by claiming an unregistered identity was never there is denied by one short path to the root.
